holidays.name: National Frappe Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the icy, frothy, blended coffee drink that has fueled countless afternoon slumps. Grab a straw and slurp away.
holidays.origin: The frappe was reportedly invented by accident in 1957 at the Thessaloniki International Fair, when Nescafé employee Dimitris Vakondios couldn't find hot water and mixed instant coffee with cold water and ice in a shaker.
holidays.funFact: The frappe is still hugely popular in Greece, where it is considered a national pastime and people can nurse a single glass for hours at a café.

holidays.name: National Inane Answering Message Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate (or cringe at) the goofy, rambling, or pointlessly silly voicemail greetings that make you wonder why you called in the first place. Time to record a new greeting that confuses everyone.
holidays.origin: This unofficial observance dates from the answering machine era, when people competed to record the most ridiculous outgoing messages, and it lives on as a nostalgic nod to that culture.
holidays.funFact: Early answering machines used tiny cassette tapes, and people sometimes spent hours scripting elaborate greetings with sound effects and songs.

holidays.name: World Smile Day (First Friday of October)
holidays.description: A global day dedicated to performing acts of kindness and helping at least one person smile. Because of how it is scheduled, it sometimes lands on October 7.
holidays.origin: Artist Harvey Ball, who created the iconic yellow smiley face in 1963, launched World Smile Day in 1999 to keep his design from becoming overly commercialized and to promote kindness.
holidays.funFact: Harvey Ball was paid just $45 for creating the smiley face and never trademarked it.

holidays.name: International Day of the Lonely Cat-Lover's Sandwich (Unofficial Cat & Cuddle Observance)
holidays.description: A playful, tongue-in-cheek day for people who spend October evenings snuggled up with a cat and a snack. Expect fur on everything and zero regrets.
holidays.origin: Social media pet lovers popularized cozy-season cat appreciation posts in early October as the weather cools and pets become living heating pads.
holidays.funFact: A cat's purr vibrates at frequencies between 25 and 150 Hz, which some researchers believe may promote bone healing and relaxation.

holidays.name: Bring Your Teddy Bear to Work Day Vibes: National Support Teddy Bear Moment
holidays.description: An informal day when adults are encouraged to embrace comfort objects like stuffed animals, because everyone deserves a fuzzy emotional support buddy at their desk.
holidays.origin: Teddy bears trace back to 1902, when President Theodore Roosevelt refused to shoot a captured bear on a hunting trip, inspiring a cartoon and then the toy named in his honor.
holidays.funFact: Studies have shown that hugging soft objects can reduce feelings of stress and loneliness in adults.
